significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that the pre-edit "principal-subspace angle / CCA correlation" predicts per-pair ripple success within 0.03 of or better than GradSim across editing methods, while experimentally restoring alignment enables propagation; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) causal mechanism. It would establish both a phenomenon—"ripple failures concentrate at 'consistency seams'"—and a mechanism tying those failures to misaligned answer-relevant subspaces, thereby fixing which fact pairs should fail and whether editing algorithms or pre-existing knowledge organization should explain the failure; RippleEdits and MQuAKE make such logical propagation a concrete evaluation target. The negative branch is also informative: failure against frequency/hop controls or failure of alignment to restore ripple would rule out representational coupling as a dominant pre-existing explanation, although it would not distinguish all alternative mechanisms. Verified-true and verified-false are sharply distinct because the claim specifies a quantitative predictive relation and causal consequence; after topic substitution, the score falls substantially because the generic knowledge-representation topic supplies neither this pre-edit law nor the seam mechanism.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "static, edit-free coupling score," which is explicitly ex ante because it can support "routing edits away from seam-blocked facts, selecting models with fewer seams, and flagging brittle facts before editing." After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion would still predict a relation—lower subspace alignment implies lower ripple success—rather than merely provide a procedure for searching for an unspecified direction. Its asserted scope spans multiple editing methods, held-out relation families, and several decoder-only model families, with uptake by researchers and practitioners who screen or gate knowledge edits, though it is restricted to "linearly-decodable relations" and does not establish transfer to frontier-scale models. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: deleting the coupling score, advance warning, and routing actions leaves only the broad topic and no comparable operational handle.
